prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a wooden counter in the foreground (~0.4–0.8 m from the camera wearer) with a bright, raised cash register on the left (~0.5 m away) and a tall brown paper bag on the far right (~0.4 m away, ~0.5 m right of the register) that is partly cut off at the right frame edge and occludes the right side of a flat counter flyer. Behind the far edge of the counter (~0.8–1.0 m away), a second person stands facing toward the camera wearer with their head and upper chest cropped out above the top edge of the frame, while the floor and a wet-floor sign further behind (~2.0–2.5 m away) drop into dark background shadow. Both the cash register and the paper bag are within arm's reach of the camera wearer and the person across the counter, and from frame 1 to frame 2 the camera shifts slightly down and right before holding steady across frames 2–5 as the person lowers their hands onto the counter edge just behind the register. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the 3D elevation of the raised register and upright paper bag from the flat counter surface and recessed floor behind the counter. However, it is unreliable where flat surface graphics—such as the credit card sticker and pink flyer—are indistinguishable from the tabletop, and where the background floor, glass door frame, and yellow sign behind the counter merge into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the person standing behind the counter (~0.8–1.0 m in front of the camera wearer, facing forward with their upper torso and head out of view above the top edge) and several objects resting on the counter within ~0.4–0.8 m of both individuals. On the counter, it outlines the cash register on the left (~0.5 m from the camera wearer), a credit card sticker immediately to its right (~0.1 m away), and a flyer (~0.3 m right of the register) whose right half is occluded by the unsegmented brown paper bag at the right edge of the frame. Across the 5 frames, the person's mask shifts from the upper-left in frame 1 toward the upper-center in frames 2–5 and their hands touch the rear edge of the register mask as the camera pans slightly right and stabilizes. The map makes the exact pixel boundaries between the person's arms, the back edge of the cash register, and the counter surface easy to trace where dark clothing blends with the dark background in RGB. However, the segmentation is unreliable in class labeling and temporal consistency: it misclassifies the cash register as one or two 'laptop' instances, the flat sticker and white register square as 'cell phone', and the flat flyer as a 'book', while only detecting the counter ('dining table') in frame 1 and completely missing the large foreground paper bag.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map tracks keypoints in the upper-center of the frame corresponding to the hands and wrists of the person standing ~0.8–1.0 m in front of the camera wearer behind the counter. Because this person's head, shoulders, and upper torso are cropped out above the top of the frame, the map cannot directly determine gaze or head orientation, though the symmetrical arm placement in the RGB context shows they face toward the camera wearer with their hands resting within arm's reach of the cash register (~0.1 m behind it) and the camera wearer (~0.7 m away). In frame 1, two separate magenta hand skeletons appear stacked near the upper-left as the left hand hovers slightly above the right hand, whereas in frames 2–5 the hands come together on the counter edge at the upper-center and remain stationary. While the map pinpoints hand contact locations in the dark space between the person's torso and the register, it is largely unreliable here because it hallucinates miniature yellow full-body skeletons inside the person's clasped hands and wrists in frames 2–5 and fails to connect the actual forearms and elbows.
